solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dimmer switch's left on … turn down

indicators.note: the leftmost letter of a word written across is its first, so left picks the opening letter of switch

parts.note: to turn down the heat is to lower it

explanation.surface: A light dimmer with its switch on the left, turned down low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dimmer' reads as the light fitting, but it is the comparative adjective. 'left' takes the first letter of 'switch's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative synonym: someone dimmer is less quick-witted, so slower on the uptake.

clue.text: Falling short of contract or promise to marry when penny is 7

indicators.note: the solution to 7 down means used up, so the penny is gone

parts.note: to plight one's troth is to pledge to marry

explanation.surface: A breach of promise case, once the money runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is 7' refers to 7 down, SPENT: the P is used up, so drops out.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: a light coin or weight falls short of its proper amount.

clue.text: Rare service misread, I agree, at first wide

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of wide and puts it at the front
misread says the letters are taken in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone misreads a word for waiting service and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes W from 'wide'; 'misread' shuffles I AGREE AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for attendance by waiters, or the waiting staff's work.

clue.text: Keep turning up insignia Territorials will hide

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read from bottom to top
will hide says the letters are tucked inside the words of insignia Territorials

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers keep their badges concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will hide' finds NIATER in the words; 'turning up' reads it upwards. Territorials are Britain's part-time Territorial Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to keep something is to continue possessing it.

clue.text: On street beside square most experienced truckers pull over here

parts.note: re means on, as in on the subject of
the top person in a field is the most experienced

explanation.surface: A road-safety note: the most experienced lorry drivers stop beside a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beside' only sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: lorry drivers stop for a break at roadside lay-bys with facilities.

clue.text: Thinking again of a sonnet I record with independent bent

indicators.note: bent says the letters are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A poet rethinks a recorded sonnet with an independent cast of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' shuffles A SONNET I RECORD with I.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun synonym: a fresh review or second thought about a decision.

clue.text: Recovered and after mounting left in V&A to be framed by French artist

indicators.note: framed by means the other pieces sit inside the reversed name
in a down clue mounting means the name is set reading upwards

parts.note: Edgar Degas, French painter
L is left
VA for the Victoria and Albert Museum

explanation.surface: Pictures recovered and mounted at the V&A in a Degas frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after mounting' reads the painter upwards and 'to be framed by' sets the other letters inside. The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something salvaged has been rescued from wreck or loss.

clue.text: Exhausted? S-shut up!

parts.note: pent means confined, as in pent up

explanation.surface: A tired person stutters a request to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered S is part of the wordplay, not a typo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: worn out, with all energy used up.

clue.text: Devo plus — extra moves for Scotland to be thus?

definitions.text: Devo plus — extra moves for Scotland to be thus?

indicators.note: moves says the letters of the two words are shifted around as one pool

explanation.surface: Political comment on Scotland's extra devolved powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' shuffles DEVO + EXTRA. Devo plus was a proposal giving Scotland's parliament wider tax powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being burdened with excessive taxation would be a feared result of such reforms.

clue.text: Self-centred say nothing first about following current line

indicators.note: following puts about after current

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
O is the zero for nothing
1st written as IST
I is the symbol for electric current
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: An egotist's habit: saying nothing at first, then following the prevailing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is 1ST written with an I for the one; 'following' places CA after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an egoistical person is preoccupied with self, wrapped up in their own interests.

clue.text: In Scots' eyes Adam's second garden

indicators.note: In puts one piece inside the other, here the letter inside the Scots word

parts.note: een is the Scots plural of e'e, eye

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the word Adam's

explanation.surface: In Scottish eyes, Adam had a second garden after Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' takes the second letter of 'Adam's', a D, which goes inside EEN, the Scots word for eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden where Adam and Eve lived before the Fall is the archetypal garden.

clue.text: Greek articles about what makes Great Britain UK

indicators.note: about means the articles go round the other piece

parts.note: A, THE and AN are the English articles
adding Northern Ireland, NI, to Great Britain makes the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Greek newspaper articles about how the United Kingdom is formed.
explanation.walkthrough: Great Britain plus Northern Ireland makes the United Kingdom; 'about' wraps the articles round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Athens, the Greek capital, is a Greek; the adjective or noun fits.

clue.text: Alternately false/true: then smart (with some self-interest?)

indicators.note: Alternately says take every other letter of the words that follow, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A logic puzzle: alternating false and true answers, then a smart move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternately' takes the even letters of 'false/true: then'. The bracket hints that the shrewdness serves one's own interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an astute person is shrewd, clever at turning situations to their own advantage.

clue.text: Father's quatrain scheme

definitions.meaning: The Aramaic word for father, used in prayer
a four-line stanza rhyming first with fourth and second with third

explanation.surface: A father's poem planned in four-line stanzas.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblical Aramaic term for a father, and the envelope rhyme pattern of a quatrain.

clue.text: Failing to see new elevated purpose in heaven

indicators.note: in puts these inside the other word

parts.note: bliss is heaven
N is new

indicators.note: in a down clue elevated means read upwards

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Not seeing a new and higher purpose in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reads the purpose word upwards, as suits a down clue; 'in' places it, after the new letter, inside heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: the lack of sight, inability to perceive.

clue.text: Report 7 June 1944 perhaps and remedy English obsession?

indicators.note: Report says the phrase is to be heard spoken

parts.note: D-Day was 6 June 1944, so the next day might be called E-Day
to fix something is to remedy it

explanation.surface: A war report from the day after the Normandy landings about remedying an English fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken French 'idée' sounds like E-Day, the playful name for the day after D-Day (6 June 1944).
explanation.definitionFit: French phrase for a fixed idea, a preoccupation that dominates the mind.

clue.text: Article in broadsheet on cast with play touring isle 'such … as dreams are made on'

definitions.text: such … as dreams are made on

indicators.note: in places the article inside the newspaper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a broadsheet newspaper
an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: touring means going round the island letter
with play says the letters of cast are given room to move

parts.note: I is isle

explanation.surface: A newspaper review of a touring Tempest, quoting Prospero's 'such stuff as dreams are made on'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with play' shuffles CAST; 'touring' puts I inside. The missing word is 'stuff' in The Tempest's line.
explanation.definitionFit: Dream stuff is imaginary, the product of fancy, as the quotation suggests.

clue.text: All metrification, if a later muddling is ignored, could be in one poet's style

indicators.note: muddling says the letters are jumbled, with if a later taken away

explanation.surface: Muddled metric verse that could pass for a famous poet's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ignored' removes the letters of IF A LATER from ALL METRIFICATION; 'muddling' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective formed from the name of John Milton, author of Paradise Lost.

clue.text: Fans of Morecambe probably do this too

definitions.text: Fans of Morecambe probably do this
definitions.meaning: Eric Morecambe's admirers would be fond of his partner Ernie Wise as well

explanation.surface: Comedy fans' affection extends to the whole double act.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British TV comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb synonym: also, in the same way, similarly.

clue.text: Labour leader speaking of reverses in branch meeting

indicators.note: reverses says the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: Ed Miliband led the Labour Party at the time
on means about, speaking of

explanation.surface: The Labour leader talks about policy U-turns at a local branch meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses' turns EDON round.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a node is the point on a stem where leaves or branches join.

clue.text: Halfpenny: Welsh character who's busy chasing Scots' ball

indicators.note: chasing puts the Welsh pieces after the ball

parts.note: ba' is Scots for ball
W is Welsh
a bee is proverbially busy

explanation.surface: A Welsh figure chases a Scottish ball for a halfpenny.
explanation.walkthrough: A bawbee was an old Scottish coin, later slang for a halfpenny.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots name for a small coin of low value, worth a halfpenny sterling.

clue.text: Ingenious outcome of air.org

indicators.note: outcome of says the letters are the result of a rearrangement

parts.note: the period is spoken as dot, as in web addresses, giving air dot; org is surface

explanation.surface: A clever result from some web domain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the full stop as 'dot', as in web addresses; 'outcome of' shuffles AIR + DOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: skilful, clever and quick in handling things.

clue.text: Dominicans' instruction?

definitions.meaning: the Dominicans form a religious body of friars

explanation.surface: A command given to Dominican friars.
explanation.definitionFit: Name for a religious brotherhood, and a synonym for a command.

clue.text: Foot — a name associated with eccentric leader in a bygone age

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the following words

parts.note: the past is a bygone age

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of eccentric

explanation.surface: A name linked to an eccentric leader from a former era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes E, the first letter of 'eccentric'; 'in' puts it inside A PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of two short syllables followed by a long one.

clue.text: Dawn French for one is in short superlative

indicators.note: is in puts one piece inside the other
short means the word loses its end

parts.note: super means excellent
un is French for one

explanation.surface: Comedian Dawn French, one in short form, is superb.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn French is a British comedian; 'Dawn' is the definition, 'French' signals the foreign word. 'short' and 'is in' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sunrise, the start of the day.

clue.text: Some define Edinburgh as a destitute state

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dictionary definition of Edinburgh as a destitute place.
explanation.definitionFit: Need is poverty, a state of lacking necessities, as in families in want.

clue.text: Using verb endings in Latin I formed imperfect tense

indicators.note: formed imperfect says the letters are made into something irregular, a reordering
endings picks the last letter of each of the words Using and verb

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson: Latin verbs formed in the imperfect tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endings' gives G and B; 'formed imperfect' shuffles them with IN LATIN I. 'tense' is the adjective, not the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a nail-biting finish is anxious, full of suspense, causing tension.

clue.text: East German stood for office in US clutching Colorado voting tablet …

parts.note: Ost is German for east

indicators.note: clutching means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Americans run for office where Britons stand
CO is the postal code for Colorado

explanation.surface: An East German emigrant runs for American office in Colorado.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans run for office where Britons stand; 'clutching' wraps that verb round the state code.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Athens a potsherd used as a ballot in votes for exile.

clue.text: … but old mate in Communist Party chose last time

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in puts a letter inside the abbreviation
last picks the final letter of chose

explanation.surface: Continuing the tale: an old friend in the party picked the final time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes E from 'chose'; 'in' puts it inside CP.
explanation.definitionFit: Both work as conjunctions or prepositions meaning apart from, other than.
